Maybe the anomaly is that the main pump MOSFET T8 gate is pulled up to +3V3, causing default-on, while spec/intended safety requires default-off. But is that strongly supported? The spec says float-switch interlocks for low-level pump cutoff. It doesn't explicitly say default state. However standard low-side switch should have pull-down to keep load off when MCU pin floating. The ATO valve has pull-down. The main pump has pull-up. Could be deliberate: pump should run by default for hydroponics? NFT systems need circulation pump constantly; default on may be desirable. But if MCU fails, pump runs; if water low, float switch can stop. The float low interlock via T3 requires IO0 high to pull gate low. IO0 has pull-up, so if float switch fails open, pump off? Wait R40 pull-up on IO0, T3 base via R39. If IO0 floating, pull-up high, T3 on, pump off. So normal with float switch open? Need switch type. If low-level float switch is normally closed when water high? Then IO0 low, T3 off, pump on. If water low, opens? Then IO0 high, T3 on, pump off. That works if float switch is normally closed (closes when water high). Many float switches are normally open/closed selectable. So default if disconnected: pull-up high -> pump off. But gate pull-up default on if IO0 disconnected? Actually IO0 pull-up high -> T3 on -> gate low -> off. If IO0 input floating (no switch), R40 pulls high, off. So pump default off if float low circuit intact. But if IO0 switch fails short to GND (water low? or short), T3 off, gate pull-up on. Could be. Not clear.

Main pump gate pull-up may be needed because T3 open collector pulls low; without pull-up, gate floating. NPN level shifter to pull low requires pull-up to turn on when T3 off. So it's not default-on necessarily; it's part of active-low interlock. IO10 also can drive. If IO10 is output low at boot, gate low. If IO10 input, pull-up high but T3 may pull low if IO0 high. OK. Not anomaly.
